name: Undergraduate Student Government
info_md:
## What USG is

The USC Undergraduate Student Government (USG) is the official governing body of undergraduate students at USC. It works to advance initiatives and experiences that strengthen community and enrich undergraduate life. Its main site is https://usg.usc.edu/.

## Branches

- **Executive Branch** (https://usg.usc.edu/executive-branch/): the overseeing body. It includes the elected President, Vice President, Chief of Staff and the Executive Cabinet, which oversees USG's departments. The page lists the 2025-26 cabinet, so check for the current term.
- **Legislative Branch / Senate** (https://usg.usc.edu/legislative-branch/): the center of advocacy. It has 12 senators, 6 standing committees (Academic Affairs; Accessibility; Affordability & Basic Needs; External Affairs; Sustainability & Campus Infrastructures; Wellness Affairs) and advocacy liaisons.
- **Judicial Branch** (https://usg.usc.edu/judicial-branch/) and **Advocacy** (https://usg.usc.edu/branches/advocacy/) are also listed; the pages fetched for this brief did not describe them.
- **Programming** (https://usg.usc.edu/branches/programming/): the umbrella for many student organizations. It has 16 community-focused assemblies (identity and interest groups such as the Black Student, Latine Student, Transfer Student and Queer and Ally Student assemblies) and 4 committees (Concerts, Performing Arts, Trojan Pride, Speakers). Assemblies provide funding, advisement and a forum for event planning.
- **Communications** (https://usg.usc.edu/branches/communications/) and **Funding** (https://usg.usc.edu/branches/funding/).

## How student organizations get funding

Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs) and USC undergraduate students can apply to the USG Funding Department. The application is submitted through EngageSC. Applications are due on Wednesdays by 11:59 PM. For approved vendors, apply six academic weeks before the event; for approved USC vendors, apply nine academic weeks before the initial payment is due, whichever comes first. Each RSO can have up to 4 events funded per semester and is capped at $8,000 per year from the Funding Department. The department can allocate up to $356,100 in a school year. Fund categories are Professional & Academic, Philanthropy, Social & Recreation/Startup (for groups first registered within the last two academic semesters, for promotion and recruitment) and Performing & Visual Arts. Funding is not guaranteed, and USG recommends applying early and exploring other sources such as fundraising, IgniteSC, membership fees and assembly funding. The funding page does not list allowable expenses or travel rules; read the Funding Guidelines and Application Breakdown.

## Senate

The Senate meets in person every week. The Legislative Branch page says the Senate meets every Tuesday at 7pm in TCC 450, and the homepage says online attendance is offered on Tuesdays via Zoom. Attendees can voice concerns during open forum. Agendas and minutes are in a shared Drive folder. The site does not give the open-forum rules or the bill process.

## Contact

USC Undergraduate Student Government, 3607 Trousdale Pkwy, SKS 404, Los Angeles, CA 90089. General: usg@usc.edu. Funding questions: usgfunds@usc.edu. Contact form: https://usg.usc.edu/contact/. Other USG resources: the calendar (http://usg.usc.edu/calendar), a project tracker, the Constitution and Bylaws, and a Get Involved page (https://usg.usc.edu/join/).

## Current services

USG's resources page (https://usg.usc.edu/resources/) lists categories for emergency contacts, financial support, advocacy and academic support, and health and wellness support. The pages fetched for this brief do not describe the programs under those categories, so confirm details before citing them.
